# In the Birth of the War-God

<note original: "akhanditam prema labhasva patyu-">
May you receive the undivided love of your husband.
</note>
As the bowed Uma was addressed in this way by those <term>Satis</term> <gloss>virtuous married women</gloss>, she, by eventually occupying half of his body, surpassed even the blessings of her dear kin.

<note>This refers to the <term>Ardhanarishvara</term> form where Shiva and Parvati are united as one body, half male and half female. This state represents a union far greater than the standard blessings of affection given by relatives at a wedding.</note>

***

Having completed all necessary duties for her in a manner consistent with his desires and his great wealth, the capable Mountain <note>King Himalaya</note>, being a man of refined manners, took his place in the assembly hall occupied by his friends and remained there awaiting the arrival of the Bull-Bannered God <note>Shiva</note>.

<note>The text notes that Himalaya acted with <term>vibhuti</term>, meaning his imperial power and resources, ensuring every wedding ritual was performed perfectly before he went to wait for the groom's procession.</note>

***

Meanwhile, on the mountain of Kubera <note>Mount Kailash</note>, the materials for decoration worthy of that first marriage were placed before the Destroyer of Cities <note>Shiva</note> by the respectful Mothers.

<note>The <term>Matrikas</term> or Divine Mothers are a group of goddesses who attend to Shiva. The term <term>Pura-shasana</term> refers to Shiva's role as the governor or destroyer of the triple city of the demons.</note>

<margin>
1. Thus.
2. From desire.
3. Kin.
4. Having awaited the arrival.
5. Of the groom.
6. Cupid/Smara.
</margin>

<summary>Parvati receives blessings for a perfect union with Shiva, while her father Himalaya completes wedding preparations. Simultaneously on Mount Kailash, the Divine Mothers prepare the ornaments for Shiva's marriage processional.</summary>
<keywords>Kumarasambhava, Kalidasa, Shiva, Parvati, Himalaya, Matrikas, marriage rituals, Ardhanarishvara</keywords>
